newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Luz del Sur sale price 3.10 soles per shr.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Luz del Sur sale price 3.10 soles per shr.

text.p: Peruvian privatization officials said the sale price of the government's shares in electricity distributor Luz del Sur was fixed Wednesday at 3.10 soles ($1.20) per share.
Luz del Sur's stock was trading at 3.29 soles at 1000 local time (1000 EST) on the Lima Stock Exchange.
Peruvians buying shares through the government's Citizens' Participation in Privatization program will have a 10 percent discount on the official 3.10 soles sale price.
The government plans to distribute 55 percent of the total shares on offer through this program, with the remaining 45 percent going to local and foreign insitutional investors.
The government intends to place all of its 30 percent stake in Luz del Sur, representing 148.4 million shares, which it hopes will raise around $200 million at home and abroad.
It is scheduled to define the precise distribution of the shares on Thursday.
President Alberto Fujimori has said the sale to individual Peruvian investors drew offers worth 600 million soles ($233 million), meaning unsatisfied demand is inevitable.
Officials have given no details on the level of demand from local or foreign institutional investors.

The Luz del Sur sale is seen by analysts Peru's most important share placement since July's successful $1.25 billion placement of a 26.6 percent state-owned share in telecommunications company Telefonica del Peru.

The former state-run electricity company was privatized in June 1994. A consortium consisting of Chile's Chilquinta International Inc. and Canada's Ontario Hydro Inc. bought a 60 percent stake for $212.1 million.
Another 10 percent stake is owned by the company's workers.
